Stated Claim / Post Context:
Kidnapping suspect accused of abducting small child is shot dead by police after dramatic attempted traffic stop on busy New York City highway

Officers tried to pull over the white cargo van with New Jersey license plates on the eastbound Belt Parkway near Exit 8.

Actual Article Body:
By WILKO MARTÍNEZ-CACHERO, US REPORTER

Published:  15:49 AEDT, 15 November 2026   |  Updated:  18:11 AEDT, 15 November 2026

New York City police shot and killed a man suspected of kidnapping a small child on Saturday night after a failed traffic stop attempt on a packed highway.

The New York City Police Department fatally shot the black man in his 30s on Saturday night on the Belt Parkway near Coney Island Avenue, according to the New York Post.

Officers tried to pull over the white cargo van with New Jersey license plates on the eastbound Belt Parkway near Exit 8.

However, the driver, who has not been publicly identified, did not stop, the outlet reported.

The officer-involved shooting happened after officers responded to a 911 call regarding a possible abduction of a small child screaming in the back of the vehicle.

An officer set up a road block but the man rammed into police and civilian vehicles, the Post reported.

Police then smashed the van's windows and tased the man before shooting him. He was rushed to NYU Langone Hospital in Brooklyn and declared dead around 8pm, the report continued.

There was no child found in the van, according to sources cited by the outlet.

New York City police shot and killed a man in his 30s around 7.30pm Saturday on the Belt Parkway near Coney Island Avenue

The officer–involved shooting happened after a 911 call about a possible abduction of a small child

The NYPD told the Daily Mail that the person who called 911 also flagged down nearby officers

The NYPD told the Daily Mail on Saturday night that the person who called 911 had also flagged down nearby officers regarding the suspected kidnapping.

No officers have been reported injured at this time, the NYPD told the Daily Mail.

The 911 call regarding possible kidnapping was placed in the 60th Precinct, which includes Coney Island, a police spokesperson told the New York Daily News.

The call was made at 7.19pm in front of Seaside Park, according to the spokesperson cited by the outlet.

The driver of the van tried to escape from police by driving against the flow of traffic, WABC reported.

Video captured at the scene showed a large law enforcement presence after the officer-involved shooting.

The footage appeared to show that crime tape had been put up and that an NYPD van had been damaged.

The NYPD has asked people to avoid the area near the eastbound Belt Parkway and Coney Island Avenue
